root_cause.text: In the md/raid1 startup error path, raid1_run() failed to unwind the md_thread allocated and registered by setup_conf() when raid1_set_limits() returned an error, leaving the conf->thread resource leaked.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE and commit message explicitly state that setup_conf() registers a thread via md_register_thread(), and the patch adds md_unregister_thread(mddev, &conf->thread); inside the raid1_set_limits() failure path in raid1_run().

agent_logs.evidence_points: The CVE and commit message explicitly state that setup_conf() registers a thread via md_register_thread(), and the patch adds md_unregister_thread(mddev, &conf->thread); inside the raid1_set_limits() failure path in raid1_run().

intent_record.intent_summary: Unregister the RAID1 thread on raid1_set_limits() failure to correctly clean up initialization state before returning an error.
intent_record.what: A call to md_unregister_thread(mddev, &conf->thread) was added inside the error path of raid1_run() when raid1_set_limits(mddev) returns a non-zero value, before the existing conditional raid1_free(mddev, conf) and return ret.
intent_record.how: This change ensures that a previously registered RAID1 thread is explicitly unregistered when setup fails at raid1_set_limits(), preventing the thread from remaining registered during early initialization failure and avoiding leaked or stale thread state before the function exits with an error.

grouping_result.intent: Unregister the RAID1 thread on raid1_set_limits() failure to correctly clean up initialization state before returning an error.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly fixes the startup error-path leak described in the root cause by unregistering/cleaning up the RAID1 thread when raid1_set_limits() fails.

candidates.rationale: This error return exits raid1_run() immediately after raid1_set_limits() fails without unregistering the md_thread created by setup_conf(), directly causing the startup error-path resource leak.
This is the error-handling branch for raid1_set_limits() failure; the vulnerable path is embodied here because the branch lacks cleanup of the registered conf->thread before returning.
Cleanup on this path is conditionalized only around raid1_free(), which means the thread resource allocated earlier is not explicitly unwound here when raid1_set_limits() fails.
This cleanup call was insufficient for the failure path described by the root cause, because the md_thread allocated and registered by setup_conf() was not unregistered before returning.

vuln_statements.explanation: This immediate error return on the raid1_set_limits() failure path exits raid1_run() without unwinding the md_thread previously allocated and registered by setup_conf(), which is the resource leak described in the root cause.
This branch is the specific startup error path taken when raid1_set_limits() fails. It is vulnerable because the branch did not include md_thread unregistration before returning.
This cleanup was insufficient on the failing path because it did not unregister the thread resource created by setup_conf(), leaving conf->thread leaked when execution returned with an error.

The core md code calls the ->free method which already frees conf.

Fixe
bic_trace_step.code_snippet:
commit 17f91ac0843b50462a9c9c8f18df962338bd3db2
Author: Christoph Hellwig <hch@lst.de>
Date:   Tue Jun 4 19:25:29 2024 +0200

    md/raid1: don't free conf on raid0_run failure
    
    The core md code calls the ->free method which already frees conf.
    
    Fixes: 07f1a6850c5d ("md/raid1: fail run raid1 array when active disk less than one")
    Signed-off-by: Christoph Hellwig <hch@lst.de>
    Signed-off-by: Song Liu <song@kernel.org>
    Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/20240604172607.31859
bic_trace_step.reason: The diff shows the relevant error paths inside raid1_run() clearly, so the snippet is sufficient. The root cause is failure to unwind the md_thread allocated by setup_conf() when raid1_set_limits() fails. In this commit version, the path `ret = raid1_set_limits(mddev); if (ret) return ret;` returns immediately without any cleanup of `conf->thread`. Earlier code went to `abort:` and called `raid1_free(mddev, conf)`, but this commit removes that cleanup path (`abort:` label and `raid1_free(mddev, conf);` are deleted). Thus, on `raid1_set_limits()` failure, the registered thread in `conf->thread` is leaked. The code does explicitly unregister `conf->thread` only in the separate path `if (conf->raid_disks - mddev->degraded < 1) { md_unregister_thread(mddev, &conf->thread); return -EINVAL; }`, which confirms the missing cleanup on the `raid1_set_limits()` failure path. Therefore the vulnerable construct is present, and the fix for this specific leak is not yet in this function.

diff --git a/drivers/md/raid1.c b/drivers/md/raid1.c
index 35b2d8646ae9..7549b0bad326 100644
--- a/drivers/md/raid1.c
+++ b/drivers/md/raid1.c
@@ -677,6 +677,7 @@ static void raise_barrier(conf_t *conf)

bic_trace_step.reason: The snippet is sufficient because it shows the full relevant startup/allocation flow split between `setup_conf()` and `run()`, including allocation of the thread and the error handling paths. The root cause is a leak when `setup_conf()` has already allocated and registered `conf->thread`, and then a later failure in `run()` is not unwound. In this commit, `setup_conf()` explicitly allocates the thread: `conf->thread = md_register_thread(raid1d, mddev, NULL);` and returns `conf` on success. Then `run()` continues with additional initialization after `setup_conf()`, such as `disk_stack_limits(...)`, queue tuning, degraded counting, and later assigns ownership with `mddev->thread = conf->thread; conf->thread = NULL; mddev->private = conf;`. There is no error handling in `run()` after `setup_conf()` succeeds: all later code paths simply proceed to `return 0;`, and there is no cleanup label/path that would stop and unregister `conf->thread` if a later step (described in the root cause as `raid1_set_limits()`) were to fail. The only cleanup in `setup_conf()`'s `abort:` block frees memory objects (`mempool_destroy`, `kfree(conf->mirrors)`, `safe_put_page`, `kfree(conf->poolinfo)`, `kfree(conf)`) but does not unregister any thread either; however that block is only used before the successful return from `setup_conf()`. Therefore the vulnerable construct is present: the thread resource is created early in `setup_conf()` and there is no unwind in `run()` for subsequent startup failure. The fix is not present because there is no post-`setup_conf()` failure path that calls the appropriate cleanup/unregister logic before returning an error.

When `raid1_set_limits()` fails or when the array has no act

Author: Zheng Qixing <zhengqixing@huawei.com>
Date:   Sat Feb 15 10:01:37 2025 +0800

    md/raid1: fix memory leak in raid1_run() if no active rdev
    
    When `raid1_set_limits()` fails or when the array has no active
    `rdev`, the allocated memory for `conf` is not properly freed.
    
    Add raid1_free() call to properly free the conf in error path.
    
    Fixes: 799af947ed13 ("md/raid1: don't free conf on raid0_run failure")
    Signed-
bic_trace_step.reason: The diff shows the relevant error paths inside raid1_run() and directly addresses the root cause. In the raid1_set_limits() failure path, the code now does `if (ret) { if (!mddev->private) raid1_free(mddev, conf); return ret; }`, which explicitly frees `conf` on error when it is not yet attached via `mddev->private`. In the 'no active rdev' path, after `md_unregister_thread(mddev, &conf->thread);` it now also does `if (!mddev->private) raid1_free(mddev, conf);` before returning `-EINVAL`. Since the vulnerability was failure to unwind/free the thread/conf resource on these startup error paths, and this version contains the added cleanup, the vulnerable construct is not present in this commit version and the fix is present.
